title: Gunpowder and Its Military Impact
text: Gunpowder, a mixture of sulfur, charcoal, and potassium nitrate (saltpeter), was invented in China during the Tang dynasty (9th century CE). It was initially used in fireworks and early incendiary weapons. By the 13th century, the Mongols had introduced it to the Islamic world, and it reached Europe by the 14th century. The development of firearms using gunpowder — cannons, muskets, pistols — fundamentally transformed warfare, making medieval fortifications and armored knights obsolete. The military superiority conferred by gunpowder weapons helped European powers expand their empires during the Age of Exploration.
